svg.text: 23 Gang of Four patterns: intent, code snippet and where you see them in the JDK/Spring. Interview ready.
Only one instance, with a global access point.
Subclass/static method decides which class to
Create families of related objects together.
Build complex objects step by step, readable code.
Create new objects by cloning an existing one.
Convert one interface into another clients expect.
Treat single objects and trees uniformly.
Add behavior dynamically by wrapping objects.
One simple interface over a complex subsystem.
Share common state to save memory.
Placeholder that controls access to an object.
Java: Spring AOP, Hibernate lazy load, RMI
How objects communicate and share responsibility
Pass request along a chain of handlers.
Encapsulate a request as an object.
Traverse a collection without exposing internals.
Capture and restore an object's state.
Behavior changes when internal state changes.
Java: Workflow engines, enum with behavior
Base class defines skeleton, subclasses fill steps.
final void run(){ a(); b(); } // a,b abstract
Add operations without changing the classes.
SOLID: the principles behind the patterns
Quick picks: Many if/else on type = Strategy or State | Complex constructor = Builder | Need exactly one instance = Singleton (use enum)
Add features without subclassing = Decorator | Incompatible APIs = Adapter | One entry point to a subsystem = Facade | Event notifications = Observer
Interview tip: always state Problem, Pattern, Trade-off. Mention a real JDK/Spring example and thread-safety for Singleton (enum or holder idiom).
